generatedProse.concept-context: Two students in the School of Sport can work equally hard for very different reasons. Performance motivation is the drive to earn the grade and prove you are able; learning, or mastery, motivation is the drive to understand sport, the body and performance for its own sake. Both fuel effort, but they part ways under pressure. In a school where the interesting questions are often the hard ones, a tricky rehab case, an unclear study or a stubborn technical fault, which drive is stronger matters.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport therapy and rehabilitation students each choose a case for the same open assignment.

Tom picks the safest, most familiar injury, the one most likely to earn a high mark with least risk. The harder, more interesting case of a patient whose recovery stalled for unclear reasons is left alone, in case it goes wrong. His assignment is competent and the mark is fine, but Tom has learned little that is new. This is performance motivation: the drive is the grade and how it looks.

Amara is drawn to the harder case because it is the one worth understanding, even though it carries more risk. She struggles with it, reads widely, and comes away understanding something genuinely new about how rehabilitation works. The mark matters, but it is not the main point. This is learning, or mastery, motivation.

Both students wrote a good assignment. Only Amara chose the case for what could be learned from it.
generatedProse.summary: Performance motivation is the drive to perform well in front of others; learning (mastery) motivation is the drive to understand sport for its own sake. Both fuel effort, but they part ways under pressure: learning motivation is more likely to take a hard case on. You can now tell the two apart and recognise them in how a student studies. With a clear sense of what excelling is, the mindset behind it and the motivation that drives it, you have the foundations to start well.

check.body: In the worked example, what showed that Amara was driven by learning motivation?

items.text: She chose the harder case because it was worth understanding, even though it carried more risk.
She chose the safest case to secure a high mark.
She cared only about the grade the assignment earned.
She picked the most familiar injury to avoid any risk.

feedback.correct: That's right. Taking on the harder case to understand it is learning motivation.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the choice made for understanding rather than for the safe mark.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara showed learning motivation by taking on a harder case to understand it. The other options protect the mark or image, which is performance motivation.
